component.name: Apache XmlSchema
component.description: Lightweight schema object model that can be used to manipulate and generate XML schema representations. An in-process Java library (xmlschema-core object model, parser, serializer and URI resolver; xmlschema-walker visitor and tooling validator) that parses, models, walks, and serializes W3C XML Schema documents, consumed primarily by SOAP stacks (Apache CXF, Apache Axis) and code-generation / data-binding tooling. The threat model is that of an XML-parsing library that performs caller-directed network or filesystem IO when it follows xs:include / xs:import / schemaLocation references. Source document is under maintainer review.

externalReferences.comment: Source security threat model; this file is a structured translation of it.

blueprints.name: XmlSchema embedded-library trust structure
blueprints.description: Trust structure described by the threat model: the embedding Java application, its URIResolver and ExtensionRegistry implementations, and the JVM system properties are trusted; the producer of the schema bytes is the attacker-controllable input position, and following an xs:import / xs:include is a second, possibly cross-origin fetch (the principal SSRF surface). Out of model: XML document validation, the WSDL parser, the JDK SchemaFactory, and test components (xmlschema-bundle-test, w3c-testcases).

assets.name: Schema parser and object model (XmlSchemaCollection, SchemaBuilder)
assets.description: Parses .xsd bytes into the in-memory schema model and serializes it back (XmlSchemaSerializer). Internal DocumentBuilderFactory and TransformerFactory instances are configured with FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING=true, but disallow-doctype-decl and explicit external-entity toggles are not set.

assets.name: URI resolver (DefaultURIResolver)
assets.description: Resolves xs:include / xs:import schemaLocation references by constructing a URL from the parent schema's base URI plus the schema-location value and returning an InputSource pointing at it; the JDK then fetches it on parse. Applies no allowlist, no protocol restriction, and no host filtering of any kind. Caller-replaceable via XmlSchemaCollection.setSchemaResolver.

assets.name: ExtensionRegistry system-property extension point
assets.description: The class named by the org.apache.ws.commons.schema.extension_registry system property is loaded via Class.forName and instantiated at XmlSchemaCollection construction time. The system property is trusted, operator-controlled state.

zones.name: Schema producers and referenced hosts
zones.description: Producers of the input schema bytes (full byte control, including xs:import schemaLocation values pointing anywhere) and the hosts those imports resolve to, which return further schema bytes that Axiom-style recursive parsing consumes.

zones.name: Embedding application process
zones.description: The embedding Java application, its caller-supplied URIResolver / ExtensionRegistry / base URI, the JVM system properties, and the JDK XML platform. All trusted by construction.

assumptions.description: A conformant JDK XML platform (DocumentBuilderFactory, TransformerFactory, SAX parser); the behavior of FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING depends on the provider in use, and XmlSchema does not bundle Xerces. Minimum Java 17 in the 2.3.0 release.

The bundled DefaultURIResolver issues HTTP / HTTPS / file:// / jar: fetches via the JDK URL handlers when a schemaLocation is followed; proxies, URL-scheme restrictions, and TLS validity are outside XmlSchema's control.

XmlSchema opens no listening sockets other than what the JDK URL handler does when following an import, spawns no child processes, installs no signal handlers, reads only the documented extension_registry system property, and writes nothing of its own initiative (negative claims awaiting maintainer ratification).
Schemas are held in memory with no built-in ceiling on schema-document size, number of imports, or import-graph depth; bounding is the caller's responsibility.
In-process callers, hostile URIResolver / ExtensionRegistry implementations, the host filesystem owner, co-tenants in a shared JVM, side-channel observers, and quantum adversaries are out of scope.

threats.name: SSRF and cross-origin fetch via xs:import / xs:include schemaLocation
threats.description: An attacker-controlled schema containing an xs:import or xs:include with an arbitrary schemaLocation causes the bundled DefaultURIResolver to construct a URL and the JDK to fetch it: HTTP / HTTPS SSRF, file:// disclosure, or jar: access, with no allowlist, protocol restriction, host filtering, read timeout, or rate limit. The model explicitly disclaims SSRF defense; callers handling attacker-controllable schemas are responsible for installing a restricting URIResolver. Whether the unrestricted default is a supported production posture or a documented dev/test default is an open maintainer question (Q12, proposed: operators must install a restricting resolver).

threats.name: Billion-laughs / quadratic entity expansion in schema parsing
threats.description: A crafted .xsd drives entity expansion during the read(InputSource | InputStream | Reader) parse. FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING=true on the internal factories mitigates the most expensive expansion cases on many providers, but not universally; whether the secure-processing feature is the sufficient intended defense or stricter toggles should be set is an open maintainer question (Q6).

threats.name: XXE via DTD-enabled JDK XML providers
threats.description: XmlSchema does not set disallow-doctype-decl=true, external-general-entities=false, or external-parameter-entities=false; it relies on FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING=true, which on many JDK XML providers bounds entity expansion but does not disable external entities or DTD processing entirely. The model disclaims XXE / DTD defense beyond secure processing; sufficiency depends on the JDK XML provider in use (open maintainer question Q6, proposed: add the explicit toggles in a future release).

threats.name: XXE inherited from caller-parsed Document / Element input
threats.description: XmlSchemaCollection.read(Document) and read(Element) accept a caller-parsed DOM; XmlSchema does not re-parse, so the caller's DocumentBuilderFactory decided the XXE / DTD posture and XmlSchema's internal hardening is moot. Reports requiring an un-hardened caller parser are out of model (trusted input).

threats.name: Memory exhaustion via unbounded schema size or import graph
threats.description: There is no bound on schema-document size, import-graph depth, or import fan-out: a schema that includes thousands of imports, or imports recursively, is processed to completion or until JVM resources are exhausted. Bounding schema size and import-graph depth is explicitly the caller's responsibility.

threats.name: Network substitution of schemas fetched over plain http://
threats.description: Imported schemas are fetched in cleartext when the URL is http://; a network attacker on the path can substitute the response. TLS validity is the JDK URL handler's concern, XmlSchema does no certificate pinning, and the caller must use TLS-protected URLs, a restricting resolver, or integrity-controlled schema sources (pinned internal mirror, checksum-verified artifacts).

threats.name: Malicious class loading via the extension_registry system property
threats.description: The class named by org.apache.ws.commons.schema.extension_registry is Class.forName-loaded into the running JVM and instantiated at XmlSchemaCollection construction. The system property is trusted operator-controlled state; setting it from a servlet-context init parameter or user-influenced config file is a documented misuse pattern, and an untrusted-actor-set value is out of model (trusted input).

trustBoundaries.name: Schema parsing and import-resolution trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: Attacker-controllable schema bytes enter through XmlSchemaCollection.read(...); each xs:include / xs:import the resolver follows is a second, possibly cross-origin fetch whose response is recursively parsed. The internal factories carry FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING=true; destination filtering and resource budgets are the caller's responsibility.

controls.name: FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING on internal XML factories
controls.description: XmlSchema sets FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING=true on its internal DocumentBuilderFactory and TransformerFactory (XmlSchemaCollection, XmlSchemaSerializer) and on the walker's DomBuilderFromSax factory. This is the XSLT-conventional hardening lever; it mitigates expensive expansion on many providers but is not a full XXE defense (a documented false friend).

controls.name: Set explicit anti-XXE parser features (defense in depth)
controls.description: In addition to FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING=true, set disallow-doctype-decl=true, external-general-entities=false, and external-parameter-entities=false, and verify the JDK XML provider in use treats secure processing as sufficient when parsing attacker-controlled bytes. A future-release change adding the explicit toggles inside XmlSchema is the proposed answer to open question Q6.

controls.name: Install a restricting URIResolver for untrusted schemas
controls.description: If the schema bytes are attacker-controllable, install a restricting URIResolver via XmlSchemaCollection.setSchemaResolver that refuses arbitrary http:// / https:// / file:// / jar: / ftp: URLs: allow only https:// to approved hosts; deny file://, jar:, loopback, link-local, and RFC1918 / private ranges; use connect/read timeouts and fail closed; log import-resolution decisions; and prefer integrity-controlled schema sources (pinned internal mirror or checksum-verified artifacts) over live internet fetches. The bundled DefaultURIResolver does not filter.

controls.name: Apply schema size and import-fetch budgets at the caller
controls.description: Bound the maximum allowable schema size, maximum import depth, total imported bytes, and total import count per top-level parse at the caller boundary; XmlSchema imposes no such limits.

controls.name: Harden the caller's DocumentBuilderFactory for pre-parsed input
controls.description: When passing a pre-parsed Document or Element into XmlSchemaCollection.read(...), use a DocumentBuilderFactory hardened against XXE, specifically with disallow-doctype-decl=true and external-entity processing disabled.

controls.name: Set extension_registry and base URI only from trusted sources
controls.description: Set org.apache.ws.commons.schema.extension_registry only at JVM startup from a trusted source; do not allow untrusted actors to set it. Set XmlSchemaCollection.setBaseUri(...) from an operator-trusted string, not from anywhere an attacker can influence (note that an absolute schemaLocation URL wins over the base URI). Run on a release-supported branch (currently the 2.3.0 line).
